title: Review: Cell fractionation and ultracentrifugation; Dissection and tissue studies; Diffusion and facilitated diffusion; Osmosis and water potential
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: CE06#t3 term and clue written for the game; PR05a#t4 term and clue written for the game; PR05a#t2 term and clue written for the game; MB02a#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: CE06#N.3, MB02a#N.7a, MB02b#N.3, MB03a#N.6a, PR05a#N.9, PR05b#N.11, CE06#N.7, MB02a#N.12, MB03a#N.10, MB03a#N.3a. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Supernatant
items.clue: The liquid above the pellet, poured into a fresh tube and spun faster

items.label: Magnification
items.clue: Size of the drawing divided by the actual size, both in the same units.

items.label: Annotation
items.clue: A label plus a short note on what a structure does or a feature you can see.

items.label: Simple diffusion
items.clue: Passive movement of small non-polar molecules such as O₂ between the phospholipids.

questions.stem: Liver tissue is homogenised in an ice-cold, isotonic, buffered solution. Why must the solution be isotonic?

options.text: So the liver cells do not burst before the organelles can be collected.
So that enzymes released from the cells are denatured and cannot digest the organelles.
So that the pH of the homogenate stays constant while the organelles are being separated.
So organelles do not gain or lose water by osmosis, and do not burst or shrivel.

questions.explanation: With equal water potential inside and outside, there is no net movement of water, so the organelles keep their structure.

questions.stem: A potassium channel in a cell membrane is open. Which statement describes the movement of ions through it?

options.text: Potassium ions diffuse through, down their gradient, with no ATP used.
Potassium ions and any other ions of similar size diffuse through the open pore.
Potassium ions are moved through in whichever direction the cell requires.
Potassium ions are carried through using energy from the hydrolysis of ATP.

questions.explanation: The channel gives one specific ion a hydrophilic route through the hydrophobic core. The ions move by facilitated diffusion, down their gradient, with no ATP.

questions.stem: An exchange surface changes: its surface area becomes 3 times as large, the difference in concentration across it becomes 2 times as large, and its thickness becomes 1.5 times as large. By what factor does the rate of diffusion change?
A strip of onion epidermis is mounted in a concentrated sucrose solution and viewed under a microscope. Which statement describes what happens to its cells?

options.text: Water leaves each cell by osmosis and the whole cell, wall included, shrinks and crumples inward, just as an animal cell crenates.
Water leaves each cell by osmosis, the protoplast shrinks and its membrane pulls away from the wall: the cells are plasmolysed.
Water leaves each cell by osmosis and an empty space forms between the wall and the membrane, because the wall lets nothing through.
Water enters each cell by osmosis, because the concentrated solution is hypotonic to them, and the cells become turgid.

questions.stem: A student draws a cell from an electron micrograph of a gland that secretes enzymes, and must annotate each structure with its function. Which annotation is correct?

options.text: Golgi apparatus — synthesises the enzymes that the cell will later secrete by exocytosis.
Rough endoplasmic reticulum — synthesises proteins that are destined for secretion from the cell.
Microvilli — beat rhythmically to move the secreted enzymes along the surface of the cell.
Secretory vesicles — break down worn-out organelles inside the cell using the hydrolytic enzymes they hold.

questions.stem: A student dissects a set of sheep's lungs. Near the lungs she finds two tubes side by side. Tube P has C-shaped rings of cartilage in its wall and stays open when empty. Tube Q has a thin, soft wall with no cartilage and collapses flat. Which identification do these observations best support?

options.text: P is an artery: it has the thicker wall and stays open, as arteries do.
P is a bronchus, held open by its cartilage; Q is a blood vessel.
Q is an artery: blood at high pressure needs a wide, soft-walled vessel.
Q is a vein, because it carries blood that is low in oxygen.

questions.explanation: Structure identifies it: C-shaped cartilage keeps airways open. A thin wall that collapses fits a vein, such as a pulmonary vein.

questions.stem: Which conclusion do the data support?

options.text: Most mitochondria are in pellet 2, but pellet 2 is not a pure sample of mitochondria.
Pellet 1 contains nuclei and nothing else.
Mitochondria are the densest organelles, as they are found in the first pellet.
Ribosomes are larger than mitochondria, as they need the fastest spin to be collected.

questions.explanation: Pellet 2 holds 84% of the mitochondrial enzyme, but also 5% of the DNA and 6% of the rRNA, so some nuclear material and ribosomes are mixed in.

questions.stem: A hypothetical toxin binds to and blocks all of the channel and transport proteins in the plasma membrane of a cell. Which prediction about the cell, immediately after exposure to the toxin, is best supported?

options.text: Its uptake of both glucose and O₂ will stop, since all substances cross through proteins.
Its glucose uptake will not change, since glucose passes freely through the phospholipid bilayer.
Its glucose uptake will rise through other routes to meet the cell's own need for glucose.
Its glucose uptake will fall sharply, while O₂ will still diffuse in across the bilayer.

questions.stem: Jam contains so much sugar that most bacteria landing on it cannot grow. Which statement explains this?

options.text: Sugar diffuses into the bacteria until there is enough inside them to poison them.
Water leaves the bacteria by osmosis into the jam, so their cytoplasm shrinks and they cannot grow.
Water enters the bacteria from the jam, so the bacteria swell up and burst.
Their cell walls stop any water from crossing, so the bacteria cannot take in water.

questions.explanation: The jam is far more concentrated than the cytoplasm. Water leaves the cells by osmosis; the contents shrink away from the wall, and without water the cells cannot grow.

questions.stem: Two adjacent plant cells have water potentials of −300 kPa (cell A) and −900 kPa (cell B). Which statement describes the net movement of water between them?

options.text: From B to A, because −900 kPa is the larger number, so B has the higher water potential.
There is no net movement, because both water potentials are negative.
From A to B only if the cells use energy to pump it, because water cannot move down a gradient by itself.
From A to B, because water moves from higher to lower water potential.

questions.explanation: −300 kPa is the higher water potential. Water moves from higher to lower water potential, so from A to B, until the two are equal.
